Why I am a Climate Change Skeptic
Interesting article, as well as the comments.

Thanks for posting OP!

I am always happy to read a Patrick Moore essay....he's a brilliant researcher.

I am skeptical humans are the main cause of climate change and that it will be catastrophic in the near future. There is no scientific proof of this hypothesis, yet we are told “the debate is over” and “the science is settled.”

This is slight of hand.

You'll notice he conflates to separate hypotheses: 1) That humans are the main cause of climate change and 2) That it will be catastrophic in the near future.

So that he can claim that there is no scientific proof of the two.

In fact there is plenty of scientific proof of point 1). That is settled science, and became settled in the mid 1970s.

The statement of point 2) is so wishy-washy that there could not be scientific proof of with, without defining what is meant by "catastrophic" and "near future".

The reason why he's trying to mislead the reader? Heartland.org. They're a lobby group paid to shore up public opinion against climate science.

My skepticism begins with the believers’ certainty they can predict the global climate with a computer model.

This is a straw man fallacy. Scientist know that global climate models are limited. They're pretty good for tracking global mean surface temperature, but they're not relied on as the only evidence.

The entire basis for the doomsday climate change scenario is the hypothesis increased atmospheric carbon dioxide due to fossil fuel emissions will heat the Earth to unlivable temperatures.

"Unlivable" is dishonest. The temperature rise we have seen has certainly been unlivable for certain species, but only by reducing their niche to zero, and having them outcompeted in the new regional climate. The word sounds like the concern is that we might boil the oceans. Moore should be more careful about how his words are interpreted than this.

In fact, the Earth has been warming very gradually for 300 years, since the Little Ice Age ended, long before heavy use of fossil fuels.

This is simply not true. Temperatures fell from at least the start of records to 1910, and again from 1940 to 1970

Prior to the Little Ice Age, during the Medieval Warm Period, Vikings colonized Greenland and Newfoundland, when it was warmer there than today.

True, and irrelevant to the discussion of whether CO2 is the cause of the current global warming.

Regional climate change in the past does not refute that fact.

The idea it would be catastrophic if carbon dioxide were to increase and average global temperature were to rise a few degrees is preposterous.

And this is the core of the denialists argument. No evidence. No science. No citation. Simply the argument from personal incredulity. Well, we can do a lot better science than wonder if we think that its preposterous. We can examine what happens to regional ecosystems when we perturb the climate. We can see what happens to agricultural productivity. We can calculate what assets will need to be rebuilt further inland. We can look at what different corals and calcifying ocean organisms do under acidification and warming.

Just deciding that it is preposterous is trying to do and end run around all that work. It might shore up the opinion of those who are already convinced, (such as those who might read heartland.org), but it offers zero by way of sensible argument.

Recently, the Intergovernmental Panel on Climate Change (IPCC) announced for the umpteenth time we are doomed unless we reduce carbon-dioxide emissions to zero.

Really. I read the IPCC reports, and I didn't see this claim. I call bullshit.

Effectively this means either reducing the population to zero, or going back 10,000 years before humans began clearing forests for agriculture.

No, it means moving to energy sources that don't emit CO2. Wind, solar and nuclear are three proven examples that provide cheap and safe power.

This proposed cure is far worse than adapting to a warmer world, if it actually comes about.

What a fearmongering chicken-little. Nuclear power, wind and solar are not a scary as Moore is trying to make out.

By its constitution, the IPCC has a hopeless conflict of interest. Its mandate is to consider only the human causes of global warming, not the many natural causes changing the climate for billions of years.

This is not a conflict of interest. If there were no human cause of global warming, that would be what the human cause is. Anyone who has read any of them knows that they do look at the proportion of the warming that is attributable to human and natural factors.

We don’t understand the natural causes of climate change any more than we know if humans are part of the cause at present.

True and misleading. We do how very well that humans are not only part of the cause at present, but are the main cause. There are hundreds of papers showing this, and has been the precise subject of many high profile literature reviews. We understand the natural causes less well, as Moore correctly, and misleadingly says.

However, we've got a pretty good handle on the current natural causes. Those in the past we have less observations of, and because we have to use proxies to estimate the global extent and shape of past climate change, it is more murky.

If the IPCC did not find humans were the cause of warming, or if it found warming would be more positive than negative, there would be no need for the IPCC under its present mandate. To survive, it must find on the side of the apocalypse.

There's no way the IPCC, which amount to 14 people, would be able to manipulate the writing of the reports, which is done by volunteer scientists. This is pure conspiracy theorizing, that is obviously false to anyone who knows anything about the IPCC.

Second, it invokes the two most powerful human motivators: fear and guilt.

Those are the two most powerful human motivators? Moore should tell the advertising industry. They seem to be wasting their focus on a wide range of motivators: Hope. Family and friends. Sex. Enjoyment. Security. Self-view.

I call bullshit again.

Environmentalists spread fear and raise donations; politicians appear to be saving the Earth from doom; the media has a field day with sensation and conflict; science institutions raise billions in grants, create whole new departments, and stoke a feeding frenzy of scary scenarios; business wants to look green, and get huge public subsidies for projects that would otherwise be economic losers, such as wind farms and solar arrays.

Wild conspiracy theory speculation. Also obviously wrong in the case of governments and scientists.

Fourth, the Left sees climate change as a perfect means to redistribute wealth from industrial countries to the developing world and the UN bureaucracy.

This is Heartland.org's (which spreads fear and raises donations) main argument. They try to put climate change science as a left-right framed thing. Community studies show that people are much more resistant to evidence if they have political stake in one side of an argument. So to perpetuate the climate change denial narrative for as long as possible this argument is very effective.

It's also unethical and wrong. Science is a method of finding the truth . It is neither left nor right.

(And its truth is separate from what policy should be implemented to best respond to the facts. That is the fallacious argument from final consequences).

So we are told carbon dioxide is a “toxic” “pollutant” that must be curtailed, when in fact it is a colorless, odorless, tasteless, gas and the most important food for life on earth.

It's only toxic to humans at over 5%. The reason it is a pollutant is because it's a greenhouse gas, and the warming has bad consequences. Although ocean acidification is another important effect.

Without carbon dioxide above 150 parts per million, all plants would die.

This is irrelevant. Current climate change is about what will happen as CO2 continues to grow over the 400ppm mark. But I note that it is also wrong. This paper has points in figure 5 for plants grown at 100ppm. They're not doing well (25-30% photosynthesis efficiency as compared to 350-380ppm), but they're not dead.

Over the past 150 million years, carbon dioxide had been drawn down steadily (by plants) from about 3,000 parts per million to about 280 parts per million before the Industrial Revolution.

Probably not, but this is not well known. It is more likely that the rise of the Himalayas has caused the atmospheric CO2 to drop, by reacting to newly exposed rock, and then being washed downstream to the oceans. Plants may have also have had an effect, but Moore is ignorant of or oversimplifying this point for some reason. Perhaps to suggest that plants will act as a CO2 sink in the future. This is a hope. (Plus we 150 million years is a long wait. The problems that this causes for civilisation will peak at some time in 100 to 100,000 years.)

If this trend continued, the carbon dioxide level would have become too low to support life on Earth,

This is doubly wrong. In the 400,000 year time scale CO2 has not reduced. It has bottomed out at the height of each glaciation at about 180ppm. Humans don't need to consider longer time scales than that, as we've only been a species for half that time.

But it is also based on his false statement above on what CO2 concentrations plants can live with.

Human fossil fuel use and clearing land for crops have boosted carbon dioxide from its lowest level in the history of the Earth back to 400 parts per million today.

This is another propaganda piece. The truth is that over the ice core CO2 history of the earth industrialization began at a peak, and is going upwards, out of the range that any species alive today has had to deal with. Quite the opposite of Moore's placations.

At 400 parts per million, all our food crops, forests, and natural ecosystems are still on a starvation diet for carbon dioxide. The optimum level of carbon dioxide for plant growth, given enough water and nutrients, is about 1,500 parts per million, nearly four times higher than today. Greenhouse growers inject carbon-dioxide to increase yields. Farms and forests will produce more if carbon-dioxide keeps rising.

While it is true that overall production is higher in a controlled environment, in the wild the woody plants will probably lose out to vines and creepers, resulting in poorer net forest produce. Additionally the lower stomatal index will reduce transpiration, altering rainfall in as important ecosystems as the Amazon rainforest.

The claim that this is a good thing requires a lot more proof. In general disturbing an ecosystem reduces the biodiversity, as a few winners choke the many losers. And projections of transpiration predict the savannahisation of the Amazon rainforest - a disaster for Carbon sequestration and biodiversity.

Moore finishes with some outright falsehoods for your misinformation:

We have no proof increased carbon dioxide is responsible for the earth’s slight warming over the past 300 years.

Yes we do. We know that CO2 is a greenhouse gas and we can calculate what increasing its concentration has done to radiative forcing. There is lots of proof that this is the main cause of the increase in radiative forcing, from many lines of evidence.

There has been no significant warming for 18 years while we have emitted 25 per cent of all the carbon dioxide ever emitted.

Nope

Carbon dioxide is vital for life on Earth and plants would like more of it.

This is obviously not true for all plants, as they compete with each other for light and nutrients.

tl,dr; Moore is wrong about everything he as written, and this piece is hitting some of the common PR group taking points of the denialist industry, knowing that it will manipulate you. Be careful not to be manipulated.
